scores.rationale: Open source, multiple independent audits, Cure53 results published
Free tier plus $40-47.88/yr family; sources disagree on exact price
No source explicitly addresses Bitwarden breach history
Secret Key design limits server-compromise impact; no breach reported in sources
No known breach, but absence-of-evidence claim
SOC 2 Type 2 and a third-party audit mentioned thinly
2022-23 vault theft, ICO fine, 2026 third-party incident

recommendation.headline: Bitwarden Families is the best fit on audits and price
recommendation.summary: Open source, repeatedly independently audited, and the cheapest of the strongly audited options; 1Password is the premium alternative.

reasons.text: Open source and audited multiple times by independent firms
Family plan about $40-47.88/yr for 6 users, plus a free tier

tradeoffs.text: Less polished than 1Password; family price figures conflict

alternatives.when: You will pay more for polish and the Secret Key design
Lowest price matters most and thinner audit evidence is acceptable

caveats: Sources did not explicitly cover Bitwarden's breach history
Several sources are affiliate or vendor-affiliated
nextSteps: Check current Bitwarden Families price and read the latest audit reports on the vendor site

contradictions.assessment: Source 8 says it checked vendor pages in Sept 2026; source 2 is dated 2023 so $40 may be stale. Treat $47.88 as likelier; confirm.
Source 1 lists $3.54/mo vs source 8 $91.99/yr; unresolved, not used.

uncertainties.text: The January 2026 Cure53 audit appears only in a low-reliability source dated 2023
No source states Bitwarden's breach record
1Password pricing and audit claims come from one source
